title: The Best Puzzles and Graphics out there
review: So excited I have discovered this escape room style game after trying so many other very mediocre ones. The graphics are better than my switch or computer games, I love how each level has a clear theme / location, and most importantly the puzzles are creative, fun, unique, and just the right amount of challenging. I’ve been let down with similar game like the newer releases of my favorite puzzle series Nancy Drew and this has been my safe go to instead. Two complaints are: The hint button is in a spot where it’s VERY easy to click on by mistake. I click it when I don’t need it often and get a hint I wasn’t planning on using. And it eats up my coins. Very frustrating. The other is not being able to take a picture of the references to the puzzle answers when solving a difficult puzzle - esp ones with a lot of colors or numbers to remember. I have to take a screenshot on my phone, use a second phone, or go back and forth in game. There should be an option to view the piece of paper or a photo taken with the clue while doing the puzzle.
author: MelanieRosebud

title: Very challenging but not rewarding enough
review: I love escape rooms so I figured I’d try a mobile app game. This was the first one that popped up and it had a ton of downloads with a good rating so I decided to try it. I am a beginner at escape rooms but I also feel I’m pretty smart and I have to say this game is challenging!! There are some parts of the game that are easier than others but I’d say half the time I’m completely puzzled and have no idea what to do. I don’t think the game rewards players with enough coins after each level. I feel like the amount of hints you need sometimes is too many for only being rewarded 50 coins after each level. That’s not even enough for 1 clue!! You almost NEED to buy coins to play, which I have. Sometimes the clues are such a waste of your coins and tell you obvious things that you already know, for example “switch 2 items on the map”. It’s like we already know that’s what you need to do, how about a clue as to WHICH ITEMS or what pattern we should be looking for? Also, sometimes I have no idea what exactly I’m supposed to be doing with a certain game. There should be clearer instructions. Also, levels might be a good idea for this app (beginner, medium, advanced). Lastly, there should be a confirmation when you go to use your coins because the spot it’s in is easy to hit accidentally and then there goes your coins. Perhaps a pop up asking if you indeed want to use a hint? For now, I think I’m going to look for an easier app which gives more rewards so that if I do need a hint I don’t have to keep spending money.
author: Grid App Review

title: Coins are hard to earn and game is buggy
review: I enjoy the game.  I can figure out most of the puzzles on my own, or with the occasional hint. There are some very hard  puzzles, and you can get hints for 100 coins each for two, then 300 coins for solution.  That could cost you 500 coins if the first two hints aren’t enough to solve the puzzle.  To replace those coins you can watch ads for 20 coins each. That’s 25 ads! But the game limits how many you can watch at one time. You get coins for each consecutive day you play which is nice, but the max is 70 for the seventh day and each day after.  So, if you can’t solve a problem, it’s going to deplete your coins by 500. It takes a lot to recoup them.  Two bugs have occurred in my game…..I had to spend 500 coins on hints and solution to a puzzle I had already solved. I was just trying to get a hint at where to go to next in the game.  I did get reimbursed for those coins. Thank you for that. But, when I was watching an ad, to get coins, the ad froze and I couldn’t close it. I closed the game and returned to it several hours later and the ad was still there. I couldn’t close it, so in  frustration, I deleted the game. I hated to do it, because for the most part, I enjoyed playing the game.
author: Meha1

title: Interesting game but needs work
review: I love the puzzle aspect of this game, mostly. There have been a few puzzles that even once I have the answer made little to no sense, but for the most part the puzzles are great. The story is kinda neither here nor there- like it doesn’t bother me but it doesn’t really add anything to the game. It doesn’t seem to matter and honestly I don’t care about it at all. Now the hints are the part that needs work. First, I think they are in the wrong order: they give you a clue first and if you ask for a new one, it just points to where you need to go. Maybe for some that is helpful but the clue for me already gives the spot away, so then I’m wasting coins on a hint I don’t need. I feel it should be the other way around- like first tell us where to focus and THEN the clue on how to solve it. Lastly, I don’t like that the last “clue” just solves the puzzle for you, well, it’s not the solution being done for me that is the problem, it’s just that most of them are done in a flash and then disappear! I want to know why/how that conclusion was made! I want to learn how it was done so I can keep it in mind for future puzzles. Please!Overall, I generally enjoy the game and can’t wait to see more stages and chapters.
author: Fruitfly20

title: Excellent puzzle escape game with LOTS of levels
review: This is a super engaging game with 2 full game sets. Each set has over 20 levels. There are a couple of story lines if your interested, you can follow along, but mostly, you go from room to room, solving puzzles to escape each rom. The downsides: it’s a view from above style game with zoom ins, not quite 1st person, but the graphics are still really good, so they compensate for that. The puzzles are nice and challenging (and a few that I could never understand (translation issues?), so much so you’ll need the hints and or various walkthroughs to get you through. There are also a few bugs. A big one is on the smaller tablets(iPad mini) the 500pt view hotspot button ends up being right on top of a couple of actual action spots so the only way to complete the action (ie unscrew a grate corner), is to use 500pts to activate the hotspot view to get it out of your way - SUPER ANNOYING. The other one is that some of the ads bogg the system down and take forever to run (if your lucky) or crash the game altogether, losing all your changes for that level.
author: Nawtee Zoot

title: Entertaining but can use improvements
review: This game is entertaining. There are some pretty tricky puzzles. I feel like it costs too much for hints as it takes forever to earn what it costs. Also it costs too much to start a level as it takes forever to replenish energy. I have completed some levels fairly quickly but the energy is slow to replenish I find myself rarely playing throughout the day. One HUGE issue I have is the placement of the hint. As I am going through a level I have ACCIDENTALLY touched this part of the screen with my palm as I am trying to use my thumbs to touch someplace else and it immediately activates a hint that I did not want to use which uses up the coins I have been saving for when I truly need a hint. Maybe change the location for a hint to the top of the screen or have a confirmation before cashing out like “are you sure you want to use a hint” so if it is an accident it can be avoided. Otherwise it definitely makes me use my brain which I love.
author: sport luvr

title: Great idea, terrible clues
review: I love escape room games. I especially love when they’re challenging. But I do not love when they rely on random guesses and not logical processes. In all of the levels marked “really hard” more than one of the puzzles has such poorly assembled clues that I haven’t been able to connect anything in the environment of the level to that puzzle. Several times I have only progressed in the game because I literally tried 20 or more combinations or I watched a million ads to accrue enough coins to skip that puzzle. And the hints are the least helpful hints of any game I’ve ever played. They say things like, “Solve all the puzzles” and “It looks like you need colors to solve that puzzle”. These are not the hard parts of the game! What I need is a clue for how to solve the puzzles sometimes. Like, how do I narrow down what elements in the environment are actually part  of the clue??? I find myself increasingly frustrated as I play this game.
author: Millie5678

title: Not For Prudes Like Me
review: I know that writing this review is kind of like trying to stay dry with an umbrella whilst standing in Niagara Falls. But just in case you’re like me and was looking for an escape adventure game that didn’t involve horror, murder, or some creepy paranormal theme. If you you were wanting to do fun puzzles that were easy to navigate and didn’t mind to spend the time watching a video to get free coins or energy because you just can’t bring yourself to purchase imaginary coins you already “earned”, this was almost the game for you. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend it due to the fact of me, being the type of person who doesn’t want the aforementioned murder, horror, or ghost stories,I’m also the type of person who doesn’t want to have pornographic images flash in front of my eyes while I wait for my free coins to download. Perhaps you would say “well then purchase the ad free option.” Naw, that’s ok. I was just looking to pass the time on a cold afternoon. I guess it’s a good reminder of what a waste of time games can be, and that there truly is no such thing as innocent fun anymore.
author: Scibbywibber

title: Fun but confusing
review: I really like this game. The graphics are great and there are lots of rooms to get through; however, a lot of the actions don’t make sense and are very difficult to figure out. For example, using a coin to loosen screws is not something you would normally do. Putting a screwdriver in the scene to find would be better. Also, many of the puzzles or combinations are hard to understand where the answer comes from. Like when you provide 9 colors and there are only seven needed, it’s impossible to get it right without watching a video and getting the answers. I don’t want to watch a video but sometimes I can’t progress without it. How would I know to break glass with another object besides a hammer? How would I know to melt something with something other than steam or fire, not a putrid vegetable. The game is great, I just feel it could be better if the actions needed were more logical.
author: Babydoll Bird

title: Good and Bad
review: Overall the puzzles are very fun! I enjoy the games.What I think needs to change:Some puzzles are too janky/clunky to work on this app. Especially puzzles where you need to slide small things. The app struggles with this and makes solving the puzzle so difficult.Another thing is sometimes when you need a hint, they force you to waste huge amounts of coins. The first clue you get is usually a hint as to what puzzle you should work on next, which I doubt people struggle with anyway. The second hint just circles the puzzle - completely and utterly useless and I believe they know it is, and just want to get you to waste coins so you have to buy more or watch ads. The third “hint” just solves that part of the puzzle for you, often without even an explanation. There are no good hints. Just too little and then too much. Would be 5 stars if those 2 issues were fixed!
author: MCB0818
